entry.title: Sekke
entry.summary: Proyecto por Victor Berriel con 20 imágenes.
entry.content:
Autor(es): Victor Berriel


Sekke provides the infrastructure that enables businesses to launch and operate their own payment gateways. The identity builds on this role, giving visual expression to the technology that connects systems, supports operations, and empowers businesses.

A foundation for progress is the concept guiding the project. The dot represents the starting unit of a structure that gains strength through organization and connection. This principle shapes the symbol, graphic elements, and image treatments: distinct expressions sharing a common origin.

The symbol brings together two complementary modules through the interplay of form and space. Its construction suggests exchange, continuity, and movement, reflecting the relationship between Sekke’s infrastructure and each client’s operation.

The visual language balances precision with approachability. Clear, structured compositions convey confidence, while portraits place people at the center of the narrative. Technology becomes connected to those who develop, support, and use each solution.

From the platform to brand communications, the identity establishes a consistent, flexible presence. A system that adapts while remaining recognizable, reflecting Sekke’s purpose: to provide a solid foundation for businesses to move forward under their own brand.

entry.title: Parisian Mirage
entry.summary: Proyecto por Yulong Lli con 6 imágenes.
entry.content:
Autor(es): Yulong Lli


Parisian Mirage
Parisian Mirage traces the emotional trajectory of modern creatives navigating between rigid urban reality and inner flux across six cinematic vignettes.

Beginning on a twilight rooftop where the Eiffel Tower dissolves into cosmic orbits to absorb professional pressure, moving to a Haussmannian foyer where a woman severs past attachments with scissors as memories shed like luminous ash toward a glowing doorway, and into a quiet café where stardust rising from an espresso cup flows into a weary mind to reawaken a dormant pencil; beneath a grand glass arcade, a vertical cascade of particles envelops shoppers in the seductive illusion of commercial magic and social gaze, before shifting to a sculpture garden where a ghostly figure on a bench weathers into the evening breeze, and concluding outside Le Bon Marché at dusk, where passersby and a lone figure appear as translucent mirages lingering in the fragile space between tangible reality and poetic suspension.
Twilight Solace
Releasing the weight of creative pressure beneath an expanding cosmos
Fading Echoes
When a lingering presence finally dissolves into the evening air
Severing Ties
Cutting loose from past attachments, watching memories shed like luminous ash

Temple of Illusion
 Caught beneath a cascade of commercial magic and projected desires
The Alchemy of Coffee
Transforming mental stagnation into a quiet spark of inspiration.

entry.title: HANNES SNELLMAN
entry.summary: Proyecto por Kokoro & Moi con 15 imágenes.
entry.content:
Autor(es): Kokoro & Moi

Visual identity for a leading Finnish business law firm
Challenge
Hannes Snellman, founded in 1909, is a leading Finnish business law firm entrusted by its clients in matters of critical importance. Throughout the decades, the firm has been a trusted advisor and strategic partner to its clients. Today, Hannes Snellman continues to offer a world-class client experience and careers for some 300 lawyers and other professionals. The firm remains committed to driving innovation, fostering its culture, and maintaining a strong focus on corporate citizenship.
 
Hannes Snellman’s brand identity was outdated and in need of a refresh. Led by the Helsinki-based agency Superson, the branding work was done in close collaboration with the client’s brand team.
 
Kokoro & Moi was responsible for the visual identity of the renewed brand, and designing the applications and materials, for both digital and physical environments. The visual identity and instructions for its use were compiled into a comprehensive graphic guidelines.
The brand’s strategic vision and attributes — visionary, human, and dedicated — guided the design of the visual identity.
Approach
​​​​​​​The brand’s defined strategic vision and attributes — visionary, human, and dedicated — guided the design of the visual identity. 
 
Hannes Snellman’s logo features the sleek and modern sans-serif Lynstone font, which has been customized for the logo. Subtle details — such as slightly right-leaning legs — add a refined touch of sophistication. The logo's two-line layout enhances its dynamism. A monogram from the letters H and S has been designed for use in situations where the full logo isn’t needed.
 
The typography combines elegance and tradition, with a functional touch. High-quality, thin-lined, and versatile sans-serif font Lynstone, familiar from the logo, is paired with the approachable serif font Aime. Aime is primarily used for headlines, adding elegance and a nod to tradition, which reflects the company's long history through its stylistic details. Lynstone, on the other hand, epitomises modernity with its clear, functional design, providing contrast to the serif font.
 
The color palette draws inspiration both from the history of the company and vibrant Finnish nature. The colors feature five brand colours along with white and black. The dark green in the palette pays homage to the brand color that was part of the company's identity in its early days. 
 
Brand images, shot by Mikko Ryhänen, enhance the personality and recognisability of the visual identity, communicating the attributes and qualities that the brand aims to convey. The staff photos, shot by Antti Rastivo, align with the visual identity, incorporating brand colors in the backgrounds.
 
One of the most important touchpoints was the website, which we designed in line with the new identity. The UX and UI development of the site was carried out by Mika Mäkinen.
The typography combines elegance and tradition, with a functional touch. The color palette draws inspiration from the vibrant Finnish nature.
Brand images and staff photos align with the visual identity, incorporating the brand colors.

A TWISTED FAIRY TALE SERIES

WICKED TALES reimagines familiar fairy-tale characters through a stranger, sharper and more mischievous lens.
Their iconic identities remain recognizable, while their personalities, costumes and signature objects are pushed in unexpected directions.
A collection of classic tales, slightly misbehaved.










- THE CAST -​​​​​​​



- SIGNATURE PROPS -
Tools, trophies and terrible ideas.





- UNLIKELY ALLIANCES -

Familiar faces rarely make predictable partners.
Across uneasy alliances, quiet rivalries and questionable trust, each pairing reveals a different side of the characters.



Trust is a dangerous game.
Partners in very bad ideas.

Polite smiles. Questionable intentions.​​​​​​​
- UNLIKELY COMPANY -

Six familiar tales, with a few things changed.
Some are drawn toward danger. Others seem to bring it along.
Each has their own way of dealing with trouble, and none of them are particularly good at staying out of it.
Put them together, and the story rarely goes as expected.


Something in the woods has been watching them.
One strange hole. Three curious minds. No sense of caution.
Quiet, for now.​​​​​​​

entry.title: The Lure of the Aria
entry.summary:
For its fall digital issue, the Loyola Marimount University (LMU) Magazine invited readers to discover opera through a personal, playful guide written by David Davila. The article moves from beloved classics to bold contemporary works, and it dismantles the idea that opera is elitist or out of reach. Opera descends from the communal pleasure of telling stories through music, and it is for everyone.
Working under the art direction of Pentagram Austin, I approached the illustrations from the same place: people. Opera is, at its core, a human art form, made of desire, jealousy, grief, humor, and defiance. Rather than depicting grand stages or spectacle, I looked for the intimate moments inside each story, the glance, the gesture, the expression that tells you what a character is feeling before they sing a note. The aim was to make newcomers feel they were being introduced to people they might already know, not to an institution.
Client: LMU Magazine Text: David Davila Art Direction: P

Exhibition design and graphic identity for A gólesz útjain – On the Paths of the Galut: The History of the Jews of Győr, a permanent exhibition exploring the history, cultural heritage and legacy of Győr’s Jewish community. Located in the historic Menház building in Győr, Hungary, the exhibition brings together archival photographs, historical documents and personal stories through a contemporary visual and spatial experience. Graphic design & visual identity: Peltan–Brosz Studio Spatial design & implementation: HEONLAB



A gólesz útjain — On the Paths of the Galut
The History of the Jews of Győr
EXHIBITION DESIGN · GRAPHIC DESIGN · VISUAL IDENTITY

Project overview
A gólesz útjain – On the Paths of the Galut is a permanent exhibition dedicated to the history of the Jewish community of Győr, located in the historic Menház building in Győr, Hungary.
The exhibition explores the community's history and its relationship with the city, tracing its development, cultural and economic contributions, religious and social life, and ultimately the persecution and destruction of the community during the Holocaust.
Through historical photographs, archival documents, personal stories and original artefacts, the exhibition presents a multifaceted account of Jewish heritage in Győr, highlighting its integral role in shaping the city's identity.

Visual concept
The graphic identity was developed as a contemporary visual framework for a complex historical narrative. Built around a geometric visual language, distinctive typography and a carefully considered colour palette, the design creates a consistent identity across the exhibition.
At the heart of the visual identity is a custom-designed symbol: the letter G, referencing both Gólesz and Galut, constructed from geometric elements of the Star of David. The mark brings together the exhibition's name and its Jewish historical context in a simple, recognisable graphic form.
Geometric shapes and recurring graphic elements extend throughout the exhibition, connecting different historical periods, themes and materials. A combination of bold typographic compositions and more restrained information layouts establishes a clear hierarchy, allowing archival content and historical imagery to remain at the centre of the experience.
The visual language balances contemporary graphic expression with the sensitivity required when presenting historical and personal narratives.

Exhibition graphics
The graphic design extends across the exhibition space, from the main title and introductory panels to thematic information boards, archival image compositions and individual exhibition elements.
Particular attention was given to typography, information hierarchy and the integration of graphic elements with the spatial environment. The result is a cohesive visual system that supports navigation and storytelling while maintaining a recognisable identity throughout the exhibition.

entry.title: Still in Motion
entry.summary: Proyecto por Thomas de Franzoni con 5 imágenes.
entry.content:
Autor(es): Thomas de Franzoni

STILL IN MOTION
Water is never still. It flows, dissolves, reshapes and disappears, constantly transforming under the influence of light and time.
Through long exposures, these fleeting movements become something different: ethereal surfaces, softened horizons and suspended moments where motion seems to surrender to stillness.
This collection explores the ever-changing nature of water and its relationship with light, space and time. Familiar landscapes gradually lose their physical boundaries, becoming quieter, more abstract and almost dreamlike.
What remains is a delicate balance between movement and stillness, presence and disappearance — a reminder that even in constant motion, there are moments of eternity.

All photographs in this collection were taken along the Adriatic coast during stormy days, when restless waters, shifting skies and fleeting light offered moments of unexpected beauty.
I hope you enjoy this journey through water, light and time as much as I enjoyed capturing it.
Thank you for watching.

entry.title: BAROQUE BIOLOGY
entry.summary:
If you closely observe the genetics of any living being, you'll see everything is much more baroque than functional. Midway between perfecting and contaminating, aesthetics refuse to be domesticated. Biology, like creativity, is immensely messy, caught in the constant cycle of decay, regeneration and return.
Baroque Biology is a curated selection of Alex Valentina’s works that explores these primordial concepts.
Like remnants found on a beach, the elements in all these pieces carry the scent of the sea and subsoil – rarities like pearls and strange shells that appear precious to the human eye, yet are merely discarded matter to nature. Like an island left to its own flow, here the aesthetics of decomposing natural elements speak of life and regeneration, as if each new idea breathes fresh life into all those that came before it.
Biological creativity will endure, no matter what happens.

entry.title: Marraud Group
entry.summary: Rebranding of Groupe Marraud, including the creation of a brand architecture bringing six areas of expertise together under a shared name and the development of a cohesive visual identity.
entry.content:
Autor(es): 🟥⬜️ Graphéine

Rebranding of Groupe Marraud, including the creation of a brand architecture bringing six areas of expertise together under a shared name and the development of a cohesive visual identity.

Marraud Group

A new brand name to unite every construction specialty under one roof

Founded in 1975 by Philippe Marraud, a trained architect, Groupe Philippe Marraud has gradually expanded its activities across the construction industry. As the group grew, new areas of expertise were added to its business, leading to the creation of six companies with complementary skills. This growth also resulted in an increasing number of names and visual identities, with little overall consistency. Over time, the group’s structure became harder to navigate, and its identity no longer fully reflected the diversity of its activities.
Against this backdrop, the group approached us to rethink its brand identity. The challenge was to bring all six companies together under a shared identity while making each of their activities easier to identify.
From a founder’s surname to a brand name

Qualitative interviews and workshops revealed a shared ambition: to strengthen the group’s identity and reinforce the connections between its different sub-brands.
The name Marraud emerged as the common thread linking all activities. Already present in the parent brand’s name, it naturally established itself as the group’s defining name. It preserves the connection with the company’s family heritage while moving beyond the founder’s individual identity to represent the full breadth of its activities and expertise.
This naming evolution made it possible to create a clearer, simpler brand architecture: Groupe Marraud as the parent brand, supported by six sub-brands whose names we harmonised around the Marraud name. By renaming each company, we highlighted the group’s ability to support clients at every stage of their projects, from A to Z. Each company retained its own expertise, clearly expressed in its name: Architecture & Engineering, Site Work & Services, Design & Build, Development & Construction, Property & Asset Management, and Indian Ocean Construction.
This structure makes each company’s relationship to the group immediately recognisable while making its individual area of expertise easier to understand.
A new name, a distinctive new wordmark

To accompany this transformation, we created a custom wordmark that turns the name “Marraud” itself into a distinctive visual signature. The word “Groupe” was removed from the logotype. Shorter and more direct, the name has more impact and firmly establishes itself as a brand in its own right.
Based on the Poppins typeface, the lettering was customised through specific work on the M, R and D. Its geometric treatment and combination of uppercase and lowercase letters give it a compact, contemporary silhouette.
The M, built around three branches, becomes the defining symbol of the identity. Its graphic design represents the group’s three core pillars: creativity, versatility and sustainability.
A tagline that builds connections

Beyond its construction expertise, the group places human relationships at the heart of its business. This vision is expressed through a new tagline: “Penser des lieux. Construire du lien.”
It reflects the group’s expertise while conveying a more human approach to construction, one rooted in lasting connections between people, the ways they use spaces and the places they inhabit.
One identity, six areas of expertise

To signify this brand architecture, we developed a shared visual identity for all six companies. The Poppins typeface became the foundation of the system, with consistent geometric and typographic principles carried through every composition.
Each company nevertheless has its own colour, making its activities easier to identify without compromising the overall unity of the brand. The parent brand adopts a refined, deep teal-blue, conveying its institutional stature and ambition to move upmarket. The other entities each feature a distinctive colour palette, selected to reflect their respective areas of expertise.
Together, these elements form a clear and adaptable system: one shared identity to bring the group together, and distinctive visual cues to help people navigate its different areas of expertise. The group can now speak with one voice without losing the richness and diversity of its capabilities.
A name that embodies its ambition

This rebranding marks a new chapter in the evolution of Marraud and supports its continued growth. By establishing a shared brand as an overarching banner, we helped structure the transition from a family business into a group capable of asserting its diverse expertise without losing sight of what brings them together.
An identity that makes the brand easier to recognise, understand and, above all, lets it build the next chapter of the Marraud story.

entry.title: ABR Festival (2025)
entry.summary: Proyecto por Loonatiks Design Crew con 29 imágenes.
entry.content:
Autor(es): Loonatiks Design Crew, 2xA Studio, Yannick Gregoire

ABR Festival is built around a modular, motion-first identity that explores the contrast between Low Tech and High Life. Through a system that combines a custom pixelated typeface with the clarity of Helvetica, and a dynamic visual language generated through code, the project creates a flexible yet distinctive experience across print and digital. The result is a cohesive identity that reflects the festival’s multicultural character and the coexistence of different sounds, rhythms, and audiences.

The ABR Festival posters extend the festival’s modular, motion-first identity into the print space. Each background is generated through Processing (Java), producing unique snapshots from the animated pattern originally designed for the digital identity. Typography is limited to Helvetica, while the logo remains in the custom pixelated typeface. This contrast reinforces the “Low Tech – High Life” concept. Each poster is not merely a communication tool, but a unique moment within the visual system—a static outcome of the festival’s kinetic, dynamic identity. It can expand across social media, merchandise, and stage elements, maintaining strong recognizability and the intensity of the modular pattern.

Low Tech is expressed through a custom pixelated typeface, where typography itself becomes a tool for deconstruction and reconstruction, reflecting the need to disconnect from the fast pace of modern life.

High Life is represented by Helvetica, carrying the clarity, precision, and timeless character of Swiss Design. The coexistence of these two worlds creates a creative tension, just as different music genres, cultures, and people coexist within the festival.

The visual system is modular and motion-first, built around four tiles:
• #50D399, a bright mint green, conveying freshness and energy.
• #D6863A, a warm orange, referencing light and natural elements.
• The “25” in black on a vivid blue #4C7BFA, acting as a digital motif that bridges the physical and technological realms.
• An asteroid-like shape, inspired by metallic window patterns from Nicosia, embedding a sense of locality.

The alternation of tiles forms a visual mosaic, reflecting the coexistence of different cultures and experiences. The pixel structure is not merely decorative but a carrier of meaning, applied across posters, social media, motion graphics, and stage design, with a strong presence and clear recognizability.
